rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ecology studies life's levels — from a single organism through populations, communities and ecosystems to biomes and the biosphere. Ecosystems combine abiotic factors (light, temperature, soil, topography, chemicals) with biotic ones: producers capture energy, consumers pass it along trophic levels, and decomposers return nutrients.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Ecosystem = Biotic (producers + consumers + decomposers) + Abiotic (light, water, soil, gases)
Species interactions: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), parasitism (+/-), predation (+/-), competition (-/-)
Energy flow: Sun → Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary consumer → ... → Heat (unidirectional)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Population vs community:** population = one species; community = all species in the area.  ·  **Commensalism vs mutualism:** commensalism benefits one partner only (+/0); mutualism benefits both (+/+).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear biotic/abiotic distinction and the 5 species interactions with examples.  ·  Structural vs functional aspects of an ecosystem are a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Lichen*** — alga + fungus mutualism that also pioneers bare rock.  ·  ***Cattle egret–buffalo*** — commensalism; egrets catch insects flushed by grazing.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m): Distinguish habitat from niche.** — Habitat is the physical place a species lives (its address); niche is its functional role — what it eats, when it is active, how it reproduces (its profession). Two species may share a habitat but differ in niche.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: three interactions with examples (2024). Diagram-worthy: interaction matrix with +/− signs.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Competitive exclusion:** no two species can occupy the same niche indefinitely — the loser adapts, migrates or dies (Gause, 1934).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Levels: organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere.  ·  Abiotic: climatic, edaphic, topographic, chemical. Biotic: producers, consumers (1°/2°/3°), decomposers.  ·  Interactions: mutualism (+/+ bee-flower), commensalism (+/0 orchid-tree), parasitism (+/− Plasmodium), predation (+/− tiger-deer), competition (−/− Gause's Paramecium), amensalism (−/0 Penicillium).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Decomposers recycle the chemicals that producers need — without them, ecosystems would drown in dead matter and starve.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Science of Home Ecology (Greek *oikos* = house) studies how organisms interact with each other and with their physical surroundings. It is organised in levels — organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere — and every environmental question of our time, from climate change to conservation, is answered at one of these levels.  ·  ## 2.
